title.narrative: Integrated WASH humanitarian response to support the most vulnerable Internally Displaced People and host community in North-western Tigray

description.narrative: ltpgtTigray remains one of the most critical humanitarian settings in Ethiopia, with approximately 700,000 Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) living in conditions of extreme vulnerability and facing sever gaps in the basic needs, such as shelter, WASH, health, nutrition and protection.nbspltbgtThe North-western Zone is one of the most affected areas affected by the war, currently hosting 636,585 IDPs of which about 150,000 IDPs are residing in collective centers and informal settlements that lack basic infrastructure. The two targeted woredas alone are hosting 88461 IDPs.lt/bgt Recent needs assessment reveal that the IDP camps are very crowded, health conditions remain dire, there are no sufficient WASH facilities and people are being forced to use untreated water from open sources, putting the entire community at serious public health risk. Water availability is major challenge as there are no sufficient functioning water sources and thus households receive water far below the minimum standard, forcing overcrowding at limited water points in the host community. Many women walk long distances to fetch water and wait for hours before it is their turn while others resort to unsafe sources. The absence of organized water and sanitation systems significantly increases the risk of disease outbreaks. Sanitation conditions are deteriorating rapidly. Most latrines in the IDP campsnbspare fully or partially non-functional, and due to recent funding cuts, many implementing partners had faced out or suspended projects, while the local administration has limited capacity to support the people in need.nbspltbrgtThe public health risks of the IDPs need an ltbgtintegrated WASH responselt/bgt which this project is designed for. Through this project, Oxfam in Ethiopianbspwill contribute to address the major WASH gaps by implementing focused interventions that will improve supply of clean water to the target communities, as well asnbsppersonal and environmental hygiene. Communal and institutional Sanitation facilities will be rehabilitated,nbspenabling IDPs to have access to dignified sanitation services. Through the hygiene promotion and community engagement, people's awareness and knowledgenbspwill increase leading to appropriate sanitation practices,nbspand personal and environmental hygiene. Oxfam in Ethiopia has conducted a Rapid Need Assessment on the ground and criticalnbspWASH gaps have beennbspidentified, in consultation with the Regional WASH Cluster, the local authorities and the other stakeholders (e.g. PAD, UNOCHA, UNHCR, etc.).nbspTherefore, this intervention will focus onnbsptwonbspworedas of North-westernnbspzone, namely Asgede and Laelay koraro/selekleka woredas, targeting four IDP camps (i.e.nbspAdi-Mohameday,nbspHitsatsi,nbspMay-Hanse,nbspSelekleka)nbspandnbspneighbouring host communities, bltbgtenefiting a total of 83,150 peoplelt/bgt. ltbgtThe project will be completed within 9 months and needs a total of 600,000nbspUSD.lt/bgtlt/pgt
